name: Altstadt Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Tyrol's largest historical old town enchants visitors with late Gothic townhouses, Burg Hasegg, and the birthplace of the thaler.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Altstadt von Hall in Tirol – located just about ten kilometers east of Innsbruck – is the largest and best-preserved historical old town in terms of area in the entire province of Tyrol. Shaped by over 700 years of history as a prosperous salt mining and trading town on the Inn, the ensemble presents itself as a magnificent open-air museum of late Gothic architecture. Narrow cobblestone alleys, stately patrician houses with battlements and oriels, as well as picturesque courtyards give Hall an unmistakable flair known far beyond Austria's borders.

History & Architecture

The town's origins are rooted in salt mining in the Halltal: first documented as "Salina" in 1256, Duke Otto of Carinthia granted the settlement town privileges in 1303. Hall quickly developed into northern Tyrol's leading trading hub and the primary shipping pier on the Inn River. Archduke Sigmund der Münzreiche set a milestone of world history in 1477 when he moved the sovereign mint from Meran to Hall: here, in 1486, he had the Guldiner minted, the first large silver coin – the direct ancestor of the thaler and today's dollar. From 1567, the mint was housed in the mighty Burg Hasegg, where the invention of the roller-press minting technique revolutionized coin-making worldwide. Architectural highlights include the Obere Stadtplatz with the Gothic town hall (built from 1447), the three-aisled parish church of St. Nikolaus with its frescoes, and the striking twelve-sided Münzerturm (46 meters high), the town's landmark. In 1984, Hall received the Austrian State Prize for Historic Preservation for the exemplary revitalisation of its historic center.

Visit & Getting There

The traffic-calmed old town is freely accessible year-round and free of charge. The museum Münze Hall and the Münzerturm in Burg Hasegg are open from April to October Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (in winter Tue–Sat 10:00–17:00, closed Mondays). Admission prices (as of 2025/2026): combined ticket museum & tower adults €13.00, seniors/students €11.00, children (6–16 yrs) €9.00, family ticket €28.00 (incl. audio guide). Free admission with the Innsbruck Card. The Hall-Wattens tourist board offers guided old town walking tours on Mondays, Thursdays, and Saturdays at 10:00 starting from the tourist office (approx. €6.00 with guest card). By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Hall Mitte or Hall Ost; parking garages are available right at the old town (e.g. Parkgarage Altstadt or Unterer Stadtplatz). By public transport: S-Bahn Tirol (lines S4, S5) runs frequently from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof to Hall in Tirol station (approx. 9 minutes), from there it is about a 7-minute walk to the center; alternatively take VVT bus lines 504 or 505 directly to Unterer Stadtplatz.

Tips

The pedestrian zone of the old town features historic cobblestones, but is mostly level and easily navigable for wheelchairs and prams. The Münzerturm is not wheelchair accessible due to its 204 narrow tower steps; the ground floor of the museum in Burg Hasegg is wheelchair accessible. At the top of the Münzerturm, visitors enjoy an incomparable 360-degree panoramic view over the rooftops of the old town and the limestone cliffs of the Karwendelkette.
